campaign: Reduce the surface of execution, evidence and development while capability and pace grow
doctrine:
overgo improves models, and itself, through its own inference and training, unattended. Every row closes or speeds up the improvement loop (measure, find the gap, train or change, judge on held-out data, promote or revert), or directly serves inference or training; otherwise it is not filed. The milestone is the loop itself (improvement-loop): from there, the scorecard's gaps generate the work. Progress is counted in promotions, not landings: a cycle that measured, trained or changed, judged on held-out data and moved main. While main trails the landings since its last promotion, rows that close the cycle rank above rows that only harden or slim it, and a cycle that cannot finish (killed, withheld) outranks every other row.

Finish partly landed rows before opening new ones. A consolidation reuses an existing owner and deletes the implementations it replaces in the same landing. A new shared component is allowed only when no existing owner can serve several real consumers, and it must remove more than it adds.

One meaningful run serves every obligation whose identity and contract match: it is written once, as one record with many readers. A run never judges what it produced, and a run leaves its evidence complete by its own contract (every protocol a suite's acceptance asks for), never half-written for a later landing to trip on.

The landing gate judges the commit; the improvement cycle judges the models. The gate's verdict depends only on the tree: unit, golden, hermetic-fixture and small-device checks. Suites that load real models, read the live store's evidence or sweep the device belong to the cycle, declared by build tag, and promotion of main requires them on the commit it promotes; a store write never changes a landing's verdict. A change's landing cost is read from its diff as three independent effects: the lanes it reaches, whether it expires the inference-surface guards, and whether it needs a pinned-media reconciliation. Lanes are the main cost, so false lane reach is cut. A surface move also expires every evaluation bound to the surface, so the re-evaluation it forces counts in its cost: surface changes are batched and land before an evaluation run, never between its runs, and the guards are re-acquired once after the last of them. A batch is one coherent change, normally one to three related rows, closed before it delays a user-facing result that is ready: an operating limit, not a gate. Dependency work is verified twice, separately: its build and test closure, and the guard surface, which stops at overgodb and runrecord. A saving is the net recurring cost removed, after the replacement tests and their maintenance. A check retires only when its replacement covers the check's actual acceptance contract, whether it moves to the cycle or is deleted; the landing scorecard reports and never refuses, so it replaces no check. The gate writes all numbers; messages name causes, effects and what disappears.

A step's verify fails before the change and passes after; a verify that already passes proves nothing, so a boundary is proved by the table row that fails today. Before a landing, what the gate refuses cheaply is run locally first: the claims check after any hand edit, the invariant tables, the rules' budget and exports, and the step's verify. A refusal found after the lanes costs an hour, and a retried landing rebuilds an identical gate binary.

Each row's rationale carries four plain lines: Serves (the loop stage, or the model or capability it runs or trains), Disappears (the owner reused, the implementations deleted, the tests retired or kept), Evidence (the run and record it reads or produces, and who else reads that record), Batch (the lanes its diff reaches, whether it expires the guards, and whether it needs a media reconciliation: three independent effects, each checked against the diff).

Landing speed is protected by observing it, not by a rule. Each structural boundary (a changed path's lanes, a package kept off the inference surface, a suite kept to the cycle) is pinned as an invariant row in one table per kind, never as a new test function or a snapshot of today's lists. At each periodic review the gate's measured lines in git log are read: the share of landings that reached no lane, lane minutes per landing, and executed versus cached package counts. A rise means a misplaced check or a new false reach, fixed by moving it and adding a table row. There are no time budgets or timeouts, no ratchet baselines, and no separate tracking subsystem.

Training research is measured at the lowest cost that answers the question, reusing what exists. Optimizer math stays on the device: host Muon on the tied embedding cost about 98 s a step, and moving it took a 540-step run from about 21 hours to 6 minutes. During training only scalars cross to the host (losses, norms, brake decisions), never weights or gradients per step. Reuse comes before acquiring: cached base losses keyed by the exact window plan, existing checkpoints, held-out sets and the verdict code, before any new dataset, pass or tool. An evaluation beats a training run, a norm beats a decomposition, and a one-time computation beats a per-step one. For a training rate question the order is: post-hoc tests on existing checkpoints, then the held-out brake from the training forward against cached base losses, then a per-layer relative step size, and per-direction spectral scaling last.

User-journey performance (owner, 2026-10-05). Optimize complete journeys, measured as action to usable result: submit to first visible answer, cold model selection to usable response, cancel to actual resource release, interrupted cycle to useful progress, with loading, admission wait, execution, publication and rendering kept apart. Start from the existing native benchmarks, allocation counts and CPU profiles of repeated reads, model loads, allocations and evidence reconstruction, and keep added instrumentation only when it explains a real elapsed-time gain. In the development loop one valid gate execution is shared by every compatible plan step and obligation, and validation and reuse are scoped by the actual dependencies (kernels, generated and embedded data, models, recipes, environment, subprocess effects); an unknown dependency keeps the broader coverage. A gain is judged against total maintenance cost (production code, tests, fixtures, instrumentation, gate work and upkeep): remove repeated processing through existing owners, and decline small gains that need disproportionate machinery. Prove with behavioral regression tests and comparable benchmarks, never a new performance ratchet, selector or framework.

Campaign of 2026-10-09 (owner): reduce the surface of execution, evidence and development while capability and pace grow. Its rows are in this plan before campaign-closeout, tightened by the lead the same day at the owner's word, for the same effect at a faster pace. Steps that change one mechanism land together: the gate's terms with its bound on growth, a session's snapshot with the review mode, a capability's identity with the stored answers keyed by it, a template's limits with its fuzz target, the codec's comparison with its adoption. A measurement already taken retires the step that would take it: of the 55 refusals the checkout records, one was a row's verify (tests 22, rules 20, lanes 8, quarantine 4) and the preflight already runs a verify before a landing is tried, so verify is not moved before the lanes. Work that only waits is filed early: the record of a landing's waits goes with the gate's terms, so its week runs while the rows between are built. The baseline improvement run (go run ./cmd/loop -improve) was started when video-request-speed closed, at 96ebdbe05, and was stopped unfinished on 2026-10-09 at 87 of its 93 cells: a run continues only at the commit it began at (cmd/loop improve.go: cycleState; cmd/validate cell_credit.go), whoever starts it here is cut off at two hours, and three commits had landed meanwhile, so a second run would have begun again. The owner asked the same day for it to be finished without waiting: an unfinished cycle now continues at the commit it began at (baseline-resume), where the 84 cells it measured are still kept, and it is started outside a session so no time limit ends it. The newest published scorecard is of 2026-10-07, so none shows this campaign's video gains until that record exists. Rows that move no measured result land while it runs: recipe-eligibility/lifecycle, session-isolation/sessions, evaluation-chain/pool, capability-identity/identities. Rows that change a measured result follow it: capability-identity/second-kind, template-bounds, codec-precision. A row's count is set from the figure the gate's preflight gives its built change, and carried in the plan of the commit before it, so no commit is spent on raising one; a count set before the row is built is an estimate and says so. Rows that move a measured surface stand side by side after it, the picture session, capability identity and the template's bounds, and land before the evaluations of evaluation-chain, not between them.

This campaign keeps Go, CUDA and HTML/JS, and extends an existing owner before it adds one. Each row begins with a measurement and fixes its acceptance before its code is written; a measurement already taken is reused when it is enough. A row deletes the implementation it replaces in the same landing; a reader that records already in the store need stays until those records are migrated. A pilot that is not accepted is taken out of the served path, and its measurements and the reason it was refused are kept.

The production growth refusal stays. A row with no allowance adds no net production code, which is this campaign's default: a migration deletes at least what it adds. A row that adds a mechanism before it deletes one carries a count, set with the row before its code and read from the commit the change builds on. An item's count is for all its landings together: each landing's growth is charged to it and what is left is what the next may add. Each count here is a ceiling, the present size of the owner the row extends, for the lead to lower when the row's first step reports. Test code, fixtures, record schemas and CUDA source are reported with each landing and not refused; a test is retired only when its replacement catches the same seeded failure.

The gate judges the candidate tree by hermetic and small-device checks; real-model quality and speed are measured by the cycle. A stored result is reused only under an unchanged identity of the code, model, recipe, data, settings and request it depends on. A request for a fresh measurement always runs, and a dependency that cannot be named keeps the wider scope. Resident resources, compiled execution and a request have separate identities, built by one mechanism into separate keys for sessions, outputs and scores. Eligibility is kept apart from selection, observations from scores, and the records that choose a candidate from the records that confirm it.

The web client and the store's log are outside this campaign.

The reward-training campaign (rows confirmation-integrity, instruction-verdicts and reward-training, with shared-numerical-program after them) was merged on 2026-10-10 from the owner's amendment, and three of its rules are carried by no row. Its order is its dependencies': repair confirmation, add the exact binary verdict and the instruction acceptance, retain sampled tokens, rank and skip tied groups, share the weighted device step, build the producer, run the one reward-against-control experiment, and only then migrate the dense block. The experiment is frozen before it trains: a protocol missing a numerical gain or resource criterion is not dispatched, and the pilot does not change the text objective's likelihood acceptance. Completing the experiment and adopting its model are separate: a complete negative or inconclusive record closes the experiment and activates nothing. And for these rows a count's reason keeps the estimate the row was filed with for good: the count is the allowance that remains, each landing reports its growth against the filed estimate, and an allowance is raised only by a reasoned change to the plan before the work exceeds it.

items.title: Run and train one dense block from one definition

budget.reason: A loan, not growth the row keeps: the row is accepted only if its last step removes more than its steps added. Measured on 2026-10-11. The first step, committed: the derivative rules and the builder of a backward graph, and the block adapter that trains through them on the host, 3,982 nodes. The device step, by the automated checks' own figure on its built change: 455 nodes, the adapter's programs run through an executor it is handed and their binding to the device through the graph runtime's resident session.

steps.title: Differentiate attention a key head at a time, and measure the block's passes on the device again
steps.rationale:
Added on 2026-10-11 from the device step's result (docs/verification/dense-block-program-device.txt). The derived forward and backward of a block take about twice the resident trainer's hand-written ones on the device, and the record says why: a step launches 517 operations, 364 of them the attention's backward, which the rule composes a query head at a time, and the passes are bound by that number. Query heads that share a key and value head need not be taken apart: laid side by side their queries are more columns of one matrix, so the scores, their softmax, the shares' gradient and the three products are each one two-dimensional operation a key head, the keys' and values' sums over their query heads coming from the products themselves. On a block of fourteen heads over two that is two passes of the rule where there were fourteen, about 205 launched operations where there were 517, with the operations that exist and none added.

The step rewrites the attention's rule that way and its causal mask for several heads at once, keeps the rule held to float64 directional derivatives grouped and not, and measures the block on the device again, replacing the record's figures and findings. It adds no code on balance: the rule loses its sum over a group's heads.

Serves: train. Disappears: the per-head pass of the attention's rule. Evidence: the directional derivatives, the host adapter's task and resume, the device's agreement with the host, and the record measured again. Batch: device. Count: none; the row has none left and the rule is to come out no larger.

steps.title: Train an adapter on a dense block through the tensor program, its backward pass built from the operations' own rules
steps.rationale:
A model's forward pass on the host, its forward pass on the device and its backward pass are written apart. Eighteen packages define backward functions, hostmath and devicemath among them, and a training program is bound to forward, backward and update functions its trainer supplies (internal/trainingprogram execution.go: BindObjective). tensor.Program is already one graph for both backends, and its planner already tracks lifetimes and aliases (internal/tensor program.go, planner).

The step first lists the operations the block uses that have no derivative rule and what replacing the block and its adapter trainer costs, and fixes its scope there. It then adds a rule for each of those operations, builds the backward graph in Go, and schedules activations, gradients and Muon's state through the planner. Attention, convolution, normalization and matrix products stay whole operations. The rules and the builder live in a package serving does not import: internal/tensor is in the inference surface and internal/densecausal is not, so the serving records do not expire for a training pilot. It is accepted when the block agrees with the model's own reference; its gradients agree with float64 directional derivatives on small cases; an adapter learns a controlled task and resumes from a checkpoint to the same values; device memory and time are no worse than the paths it replaces; and production code is smaller after the new rules are counted, which is why the row carries no allowance. The code it replaces is in densecausal (3,100 lines), densecausaltrain (407) and loratrain (536), the LoRA trainer on the dense model. If it is not accepted it is taken out of the served path and its measurements are kept. A second family, chosen by how much it deletes and how many rules it shares, is filed only on that result.

Serves: train. Disappears: the block's separate host, device and backward code, and the LoRA trainer's. Evidence: the five comparisons above. Batch: device; it reruns the training proofs of the trainers it touches and expires no inference guard.

Ordering for this amendment: implement reward-training/weighted-step first, then complete reward-training/first-run before migrating the numerical implementation. Completion of that experiment may be negative or inconclusive and does not require adoption. Reuse the weighted-step boundary and its masks, signed weights, normalization, optimizer-state and resume contracts; the graph migration changes their implementation rather than creating a second training API. Re-run those existing contracts as part of this row's training proofs. Preserve the original numerical, gradient, resume, memory, time and net-reduction acceptance above.

Scope, fixed on 2026-10-11 from a reading of the code (the row's first act). No operation has a derivative rule: nothing in internal/tensor, its reference executor, its planner or internal/model derives anything, and every backward pass is written by hand in hostmath, devicemath and the trainers. The program's operations are closed to internal/tensor, which is in the inference surface: a package outside it can only compose the 65 that exist. Of what a block needs, the forward of every operation exists as one (MulMat, RMSNorm with Multiply, SiLU, Attention, RoPENeoX, Add, Scale, GetRows, the low-rank path of MulMat) except cross-entropy, and no backward does. So the rules compose existing operations and add none, and no serving record expires: a product's transpose products; RMS normalization's from its own output, the row's root mean square being the row sum of output times input over the width; SiLU's from Sigmoid; RoPE's by its Reverse option, which is its transpose; attention's from scores, a causal mask fed as an input, Softmax and products, with the heads of a group summed; and the loss's gradient as Softmax less a fed one-hot, scaled a row. Attention, normalization and products stay whole operations going forward. The embedding's scatter has no operation and is not needed while the table is frozen, which an adapter's training leaves it. What the row replaces is larger than it counted: internal/densecausal is 3,193 lines, of which the block's forward and backward are 713 and the rest is loaders, the preference and reward trainers, the mixture model and the graft, all standing on the layer's backward; densecausaltrain is 501; loratrain is 536; and the block's device code in devicemath, about 1,160 lines, is not in the row's count. Three things the row assumed do not hold and are decided here. The planner plans one execution's intermediates and has no state that lasts across steps, so weights, gradients gathered over a group and Muon's state stay buffers the trainer owns and are bound as inputs and retained outputs; the planner schedules a step's activations and gradients and nothing else. The reference executor is 32-bit, so a float64 directional derivative is taken from a float64 block written in the test, as the device layer's test does, and not from the program. And the allowance: the steps before the last add the rules and the two trainers before anything is deleted, so each carries a measured count, and the row is accepted only if the last step removes more than they added.

Steps. rules: derivative rules for the block's operations and the builder of a backward graph, in a package the inference surface does not import, held to float64 directional derivatives on small cases. host-block: an adapter trained on one dense block through the program on the host, agreeing with the model's own reference, learning a controlled task and resuming to the same values. device-block: the same program on the device, its memory and time set beside the paths it replaces. dense-block: the acceptance, and on it the replacement and the deletions, or the removal from the served path with the measurements kept.

steps.title: Commit the candidates of several worktrees through one queue
steps.rationale:
With one implementing session to a worktree, each submits a fixed candidate with its base commit and its row. The queue integrates it onto master, checks the tree that results, advances master and removes the row, so sessions do not conflict in docs/plan.json. The terms a candidate is judged by are those of the master commit it is integrated onto, not those of the commit it was written against: a row's terms change only by a commit of their own, which the lead makes, and a candidate that no longer meets them is refused and says which term moved. Its test starts two sessions from one base and holds that neither is charged with the other's files, that the second is checked on the tree the first left and by the terms that tree holds, and that a queue stopped and started again loses no candidate and removes no row twice. The device and the outputs sessions share stay under their present locks: worktrees do not add a second device. It waits on the owner's decision.

Serves: change. Disappears: the rule that one session commits for a checkout. Evidence: two sessions' landings on one day, neither touching the other's files, and the waits before and after. Batch: host, device and webui.

items.title: Retire the host's reward trainer once the workbench trains rewards on the device or stops offering them

steps.title: Retire the host's reward trainer once the workbench trains rewards on the device or stops offering them
steps.rationale:
The reward-training campaign's weighted-step asked for the production host reward trainer, densecausal TrainGRPOGroupsResume, to be deleted in its own landing, with only reference fixtures and historical readers kept. That landing, 591a84b04, gave the device one weighted step for fine-tuning and rewards and sent every reward session not held to the host to it, and kept the host trainer for a session that is held to the host. The reason is the workbench: the server trains on the host alone (internal/server trainsOnHost), its training workspace admits the reward objective, and with the host trainer gone a reward run from the workbench would be refused with nothing in its place. Deleting a served capability was not the lead's to do inside a numerical step.

What retires it. Either the workbench trains rewards through the device's weighted step, which the row gui-resident-model-fit prepares for by deciding what stays resident beside a device training run, or the owner decides the workbench does not train rewards and the server stops admitting the objective. Then the workflow's host branch for the reward objective and TrainGRPOGroupsResume are deleted, the host calculation staying only as the reference the device test is held to (internal/densecausaltrain TestOneWeightedStepServesFineTuningAndRewards), and a reward session held to the host is refused with the reason.

Until then there are two production routes for a reward session, the device's and the host's, which give the same losses to a millionth and weights as close as fine-tuning's two routes are; the campaign's experiment runs on the device.

Serves: train from rewards through one numerical owner.
Disappears: the production host reward update and the workflow's branch to it.
Evidence: a reward session held to the host refused, the workbench's reward run on the device or the objective no longer admitted there, and the device test still held to the host's calculation.
Batch: host, and the workbench's own tests.

Decided on 2026-10-11, when the row was reached, under the owner's instruction not to wait for a decision: the lead takes the first way. The workbench keeps the reward objective and comes to train it on the device, so this row awaits gui-resident-model-fit and stands after it. decisions.question: The scorecard's serving cells (first-output, throughput, load-time, peak-device-memory) aggregate every attempt a recipe ever made: medians over all time, total tokens over total decode time, the highest peak ever. A landed improvement shows only as old samples are outnumbered and a peak never falls. Since delete-selection each cycle measures every serving cell once at the measured commit. Should those cells read the newest successful measured attempt instead, accepting one sample's timing noise in each cycle's moved list?
options: newest measured attempt
all-time aggregates
median of the newest few attempts
decisions.recommendation: newest measured attempt
decisions.answer: newest measured attempt

decisions.question: Held-out quality is unscored for forecast, image-embedding, image-gen, seq2seq, tabular and vqa because each needs a held-out set the store lacks. Answering authorizes exactly these downloads into the datasets root, each to be verified by hash once fetched: ETTh1 (github.com/zhouhaoyi/ETDataset, 2.6 MB, forecast); BFCL v3 simple (gorilla-llm/Berkeley-Function-Calling-Leaderboard, 0.3 MB, seq2seq); BeyondArena credit-g (TabArena/BeyondArena, 0.2 MB, tabular); TIFA v1.0 (github.com/Yushi-Hu/tifa, 10 MB, image-gen); A-OKVQA validation (HuggingFaceM4/A-OKVQA, 60 MB, vqa); Imagenette 160 px (fast.ai imagenette2-160, 100 MB, image-embedding). About 173 MB in all. The other five unscored rows (generation, projection, speech, training, video-gen) use sets already on disk and are not blocked.
options: Download all six (about 173 MB)
Download only the four under 11 MB (ETTh1, BFCL, credit-g, TIFA)
Download none and score only what is on disk
decisions.recommendation: Download all six (about 173 MB)
decisions.answer: Download only the four under 11 MB (ETTh1, BFCL, credit-g, TIFA)

decisions.question: Editing a pinned media runtime path (go.mod, kernels, internal/cuda, tensor, devicemath and the rest of docs/image_video_merged.json's runtime paths) needs a reviewed delta: a device receipt, a delta entry, and the registry's identity pinned in a test, built by hand twice on 2026-10-04 and again for every kernel row ahead (e4b-decode-graph, decode-small-kernels). It exists so media evidence acquired at the pinned runtime stays valid across an output-neutral edit. Since the cycle re-acquires every media cell at the commit it promotes, and its models lane runs the media acceptance tests against the frozen references, the evidence that gate protects is re-proved every cycle: it is the same per-cell currency check validate-currency deleted. Retire the registry, its pin and the gate-time check (about 600 lines of test code, the registry JSON and the landing's pinned-path rule), or keep it and build a one-command tool for it (row media-delta-command)?
options: Retire the pin, the registry and the gate-time check; the cycle's media acceptance holds the contract
Keep the pin and build the one-command delta tool (media-delta-command)
decisions.recommendation: Retire the pin, the registry and the gate-time check; the cycle's media acceptance holds the contract
decisions.answer: Retire the pin, the registry and the gate-time check; the cycle's media acceptance holds the contract

decisions.question: Speech, image-gen and video-gen quality cannot be scored by the model alone: pocket-tts outputs audio, the image generators pictures, Wan2.1 and Un-0 clips. Each proposal scores the output by a second local model: a speech recognizer for round-trip word error rate, a vision-language model for TIFA questions and for matching a clip to its caption. evaluate has no suite in which a generator's output is judged by another model, and a record must name both the generator's recipe, which the scorecard reads, and the judge's identity, which the score depends on. One judged-generation suite kind (the projection session already shows a video to Qwen3.8-27B) would serve all three rows and their eight models, with a new session for each judge modality.
options: Build one judged-generation suite kind for speech, image-gen and video-gen
Score speech by its recognizer round trip only, and leave image-gen and video-gen unscored
Leave all three unscored
decisions.recommendation: Build one judged-generation suite kind for speech, image-gen and video-gen
decisions.answer: Build one judged-generation suite kind for speech, image-gen and video-gen

decisions.question: Held-out quality of training is scored for a recipe only by a train -objective session, which publishes a held-out verdict. Qwen2.5-0.5B trains through that route and now has its verdict (a token-prediction objective over a held-out third of the WikiText-2 articles). The other six training recipes belong to routes that prove the route rather than score text: Qwen3.5-4B and 9B hybrid-stack (a bounded observed full-stack run whose evidence is that loss descends), Wan2.1 and LiveEdit dit, Hy-Embodied mot. None of those routes holds out data or scores a model, and a token-prediction objective does not fit a diffusion or a mixture-of-transformers model. Scoring them means giving each route a held-out objective of its own (days of work each, and a 20-step proof run's held-out value says little). Which do you want?
options: Declare the proof-route recipes' held-out quality not applicable, stating that their sessions prove a route
Give each proof route a held-out objective and score its recipe
Leave the proof-route recipes unscored
decisions.recommendation: Declare the proof-route recipes' held-out quality not applicable, stating that their sessions prove a route
decisions.answer: Declare the proof-route recipes' held-out quality not applicable, stating that their sessions prove a route

decisions.question: identity-carry was filed to carry an evaluation only while the code it depends on is unchanged and to delete the sampled replay. Measured 2026-10-09: 46 of the 87 newest results stand on a replay-carried result, 30 of them carried 19 or 20 times; scoring those 46 in full took 13 hours 55 minutes; the code an evaluation depends on changed on 112 of the last 300 commits and cycles lie hundreds of commits apart, so with the replay deleted every cycle scores them all again, about 14 hours more a cycle. The replay's sample is the same 32 cases every time, so a change that misses them is never seen. What should carrying do?
options: Carry under an unchanged identity, else by a replay whose sample changes each time
Carry only under an unchanged identity and score the rest in full every cycle
Leave carrying as it is
decisions.recommendation: Carry under an unchanged identity, else by a replay whose sample changes each time
decisions.answer: Carry only under an unchanged identity and score the rest in full every cycle

decisions.question: evaluation-chain's last step, acceptance, adds a memory ceiling and a speed target to a held-out pool's acceptance and has a confirmation refuse a candidate with no resource comparison against the base within them. Every candidate the proposer makes today is other weights of the base's shape, so it has the base's memory and speed, and no row in the plan makes another kind of candidate; a served recipe's memory and speed are already read by the scorecard and by the routing decision. When should the step be built?
options: When the first candidate whose memory or speed differs from its base's is proposed
Now, ahead of such a candidate
Not at all: leave memory and speed to the scorecard and the routing decision
decisions.recommendation: When the first candidate whose memory or speed differs from its base's is proposed
decisions.answer: When the first candidate whose memory or speed differs from its base's is proposed

decisions.question: The video codec can now convolve a clip of about ten frames or more through NVIDIA's cuDNN. Measured beside another job on the device: a decode about a third faster, an encode about a fifth, the decoder holding 6.0 GiB where it held 9.6, and every value within one of 255 levels of what overgo's own kernels give. It does so only on a machine where cuDNN is on the search path or in the bin directory CUDA_PATH names. This machine's only copy is inside a Python environment, so it still serves by the kernels and the automated checks skip the library's tests. Installing it is yours to do: cuDNN 9 for CUDA 12, about 800 MB, from NVIDIA under NVIDIA's license. The frozen video clips are the kernels' bytes, and I would accept them again under the library afterwards. Install it here?
options: Install cuDNN 9 here; the lead accepts the frozen video clips again under it
Keep this machine on the kernels; the library stays for machines that have it
Take the library's path back out
decisions.recommendation: Install cuDNN 9 here; the lead accepts the frozen video clips again under it
decisions.answer: Install cuDNN 9 here; the lead accepts the frozen video clips again under it

decisions.question: Should the text objective eventually change from mean per-document likelihood improvement to the frequency of document wins? Many small wins can coexist with a materially worse mean. The instruction-following pilot does not require this change.
options: Keep the current likelihood objective; decide any replacement only after calibration in likelihood units
Authorize a separate proposal for document-win frequency with an explicit magnitude safeguard and its own calibration
decisions.recommendation: Keep the current likelihood objective; decide any replacement only after calibration in likelihood units
decisions.answer: Keep the current likelihood objective; decide any replacement only after calibration in likelihood units
